label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Dear Appa, Amma, Kiran and Divya,

Before anything else, I want to say how genuinely thrilled I am that Amma and Appa are coming. The children are beside themselves, and I love the thought of having them here for a whole summer.

Kiran, you are right that you should have been brought into this before the visa paperwork started. I’m sorry. The agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, so I began getting those together, and that is exactly when I should have rung you. Instead, I got carried away with the practical side and left you to hear about a plan that was already moving. That’s on me.

For the sequence of events: the idea originally came from Appa, on the phone in August, when Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on video and Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” We talked about it after that, but explaining how it began doesn’t change the fact that I should have included you sooner.

Your concerns about Appa’s heart are entirely fair, and they need proper arrangements rather than reassurance. Dr. Prakash has agreed to do a full review in March before they fly, and a video consult in July while they are here. He is also happy to share his notes with me. I’ve obtained a travel-insurance quote that explicitly includes pre-existing cardiac cover; it is about £640 each for the six months, and the agent says it covers Appa’s stent. I’ll get the policy wording, exclusions and claims process in writing and share them so we are not relying on a verbal assurance. They will be visitors, so I am not assuming that routine NHS treatment will be free.

If anything urgent did happen, Leicester Royal is 15 minutes from our house, and I know much of the cardiology team there. That doesn’t remove the risk, of course, but it does mean I understand the system and can help coordinate things quickly.

The visa is the UK long-term visitor visa, which allows a maximum of six months per visit. The plan is for this first stay to run from the first week of April to the end of September 2027.

Kiran, your point about Amma is fair too. Six months is much longer than six weeks, and I don’t want her to feel she has promised to endure it if she is homesick. Their return ticket will be flexible, and she can go home at any time. They will also have their own space here: the annexe at the back is finished, all on the ground floor with no steps, and it has its own shower with a grab rail. They can be with us without being on top of us, or us on top of them.

I don’t want Pune simply to lose Ganesh Chaturthi either. Could we consider two options? Amma and Appa could fly from Leicester to Pune in September, celebrate with you and finish their trip there, flying home from Pune. Alternatively, you could all come to Leicester in August and we could have that part of the summer together. If you choose August, I’d like to cover the Pune family’s flights.

Perhaps we can talk properly on a family video call this Sunday at 4pm UK time / 9.30pm India time? I’d rather hear everyone’s thoughts together than try to settle it all by email.

Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, which includes “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”. So the excitement here is very real indeed. I’m looking forward to Appa’s drumsticks, Amma’s pickles, and having them with us — and to working out the remaining details together.

Lots of love,  
Meera
